policy_title: Stop Illegal Migrants by Removing to Rwanda
stated: The Conservative Party will establish a deterrent by continually removing illegal migrants to Rwanda with regular flights, starting in July, and bringing the Illegal Migration Act into force to end legal challenges and clear the asylum backlog within six months.

source.quote: Stop the boats by removing illegal migrants to Rwanda. ...We will run a relentless, continual process of permanently removing illegal migrants to Rwanda with a regular rhythm of flights every month, starting this July, until the boats are stopped.

bearing_set.reason: The policy is directly a border-security and national-security measure — deterring illegal entry, establishing removal flights, and clearing an asylum backlog; these sit squarely within O5's indicators of national security posture and border control.

Bringing the Illegal Migration Act into force explicitly to 'end legal challenges' removes judicial oversight of removals; the UK Supreme Court found the Rwanda scheme unlawful partly on ECHR/human-rights grounds, making due process and the legal-rights framework directly at stake for those subject to removal.

The Illegal Migration Act includes indefinite detention powers for illegal arrivals pending removal; expanding state detention authority without time limit is a direct coercive-state-power effect on the O10 indicators.

The Rwanda scheme has already cost the UK hundreds of millions before a single flight departed; regular scheduled removals at scale add substantial recurring expenditure with highly uncertain deterrence returns, materially affecting the funded-vs-borrowed and debt-path indicators.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn real verdicts: O5 (the intended protective/justice benefit), O9 and O10 (separate but concurrent rights costs from ending legal challenges and expanding detention), and O12 (documented fiscal cost). Community-cohesion (O15) effects are too indirect and contested to pin to a specific mechanism and indicator at this stage.
